title: Businesses only care about 3 things: Money, Time, Focus  #artificialintelligence
lesson: A buyer evaluates the destination and business outcome; the technology is the means of getting there.
opening: The presenter names three business priorities, promising a simpler way to sell AI work. This is a spoken opening carried by a face; the early money badge is partly clipped and is not a strong standalone visual hook.
story_arc: State buyer priorities → demonstrate destination versus interchangeable vehicles → return to interpret the analogy → reject the technical feature pitch → visualize leads without ads → restate the outcome rule.
payoff: The taxi analogy earns the outcome-over-tool lesson. The bot and envelopes illustrate a proposed service; they do not establish qualified leads or customer results.
selection_reason: Adds a coherent multi-picture analogy, a negative example, and an evolving system scene. It also shows why long presenter holds can coexist with fast visual runs. N30 reuses the outreach scene, so it is not counted as independent evidence here.
review_limits: Complete chronological 0.5-second source-frame sheets and machine-timed transcript inspected; listed native strips refine selected motions. No audio audition or uninterrupted realtime playback. Image-to-words reasoning is editorial interpretation, not known creator intent or retention evidence. Interval boundaries are approximate unless a native frame is cited.

beats.spoken_idea: The first possible vehicle is a Prius.
beats.visible: Map shrinks, then a labelled car grows inside the unchanged monitor.
beats.why_this_picture: Swapping the means while retaining the scenario sets up the lesson that the destination matters more.
beats.camera_observation: Native frames: map shrinks by 11.455; car appears at 11.655 and is larger by 11.998. This is object scaling, not camera zoom.
beats.camera_reason: Retires the destination graphic after establishing it, then focuses the first alternative.
beats.pacing_reason: Short shrink/grow action connects the two states; let the car become recognizable.
beats.handoff: Vehicle slot is reused for the next option.
beats.implementation_note: The two-slot condense/reshape mechanism can handle object replacement. Provide map/car assets and retain a separate monitor host.
beats.transfer: When replacing an object while preserving the conceptual stage.

beats.spoken_idea: A Tesla is another possible vehicle.

beats.handoff: Another alternative takes the same position.
beats.implementation_note: Use slotted vehicle images and wrappers that preserve their shape. A plain replacement may be simpler than adding carousel chrome.

beats.pacing_reason: The final contrasting image completes the analogy before explanation resumes.

beats.spoken_idea: What matters is arriving quickly, cheaply and without stress.
beats.visible: Full presenter; key outcome words appear in yellow captions.
beats.change: Analogy ends; close human explanation resumes.
beats.why_this_picture: The person interprets what the map and vehicle swaps meant, closing the loop for the viewer.
beats.camera_observation: A cut returns to full presenter at native frame 436, PTS 14.560; frame 435 still shows the carriage. Presenter framing then holds.
beats.camera_reason: Return to the person for judgment, not another literal taxi illustration.
beats.pacing_reason: About five seconds is justified by the three-part interpretation; no automatic two-second layout replacement.
beats.handoff: The same person applies the rule to selling AI.
beats.implementation_note: Keep the explanatory line and its natural performance; selective caption emphasis only.
beats.transfer: After an analogy, when its relevance needs one clear sentence.
beats.caution: Outcome words are emphasis, not independently proven results.
beats.time_confidence: Start refined by individual native frames 435 and 436 at the carriage-to-presenter cut; other boundary remains approximate from 0.5-second context.

beats.spoken_idea: Sell the result, not the AI mechanism.
beats.visible: Presenter with red/green comparison pills near the lower edges; much of their text is clipped or hard to read.
beats.change: Additional labels appear during the same presenter explanation.
beats.why_this_picture: A contrast label could reinforce the decision, but the sampled source’s unreadable pills contribute little.
beats.camera_observation: Mostly held presenter; overlay placement changes rather than a meaningful camera move.
beats.camera_reason: There is no clear information benefit from the clipped decorations.
beats.pacing_reason: The verbal argument is doing the work during this long hold.
beats.handoff: A real-looking workflow becomes the negative example.
beats.implementation_note: Use a clean presenter hold or a tested legible comparison treatment only if it adds information.
beats.transfer: As a cautionary comparison for overlay QA.
beats.caution: Do not copy a bad example merely because it belongs to the reference creator.

beats.pacing_reason: Briefly establish the dense whole; the next crop supplies detail.
beats.handoff: Same technical environment moves to a configuration view.
